title: Cross-functional launch checklist and cut criteria for API / Console / Runtime release
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: Produce a single, executable release-train plan that coordinates scope lock, cut criteria, release notes, and GTM tasks across API (hosted), Console (observability + operations), and Runtime (serving engine). Deliverables: milestones calendar, scope-lock rules, explicit cut criteria per product area, a templated release-notes artifact, and a prioritized GTM checklist with owners.
milestones: 2026-02-15 - Feature freeze: all feature PRs targeting the train must be merged into feature branch or deferred. Exceptions require written approval from PM+ENG leads.
2026-02-20 - Internal validation window opens: QA and interoperability tests run across API/Console/Runtime integration matrix.
2026-02-26 - Docs & Release Notes draft due: initial release-notes draft and Console banners prepared.
2026-03-02 - Final regression & load run: end-to-end perf tests at target QPS and latency SLOs.
2026-03-05 - Cut decision meeting: cross-team go/no-go using cut criteria checklist.
2026-03-10 - Release candidate promoted and scheduled for deployment to hosted and Dedicated staging clusters.
scope_lock_rules: All non-critical feature additions after Feature freeze require a documented risk assessment and sign-off from PM + ENG + SRE.
Bug fixes labeled P0/P1 may ship after freeze only if a reproducer + regression test + short remediation plan are attached.
Performance-related changes to Runtime kernels or batching logic must pass predefined microbenchmarks before being merged post-freeze.
Console dashboard changes that alter telemetry or billing calculations require a parallel data-validation plan before merge.
cut_criteria: Functional completeness: core API endpoints and Console flows required by PRD are implemented and verified.
Quality gates: no open P0 defects; P1 defects must have scheduled remediation within the next sprint and documented user impact.
Stability: 72-hour soak on staging with error rate < 0.1% and tail latency under SLO targets for three consecutive runs.
Performance: Runtime must meet documented throughput/loss tradeoffs for the default model profile; regressions >10% require rollback plan.
Docs & release notes: Release notes approved by comms and engineering with at least one user-facing example for each breaking or opt-in change.
Security & compliance: Any change touching data residency, KMS, RBAC, or audit logs must complete security review and attestation.
release_notes_process: Single-source release notes stored in the shared Drive template. Product PM drafts high-level bullets; Eng lead contributes detailed migration/compatibility notes; Docs performs copy edits and examples; Comms finalizes customer-facing messaging. The final artifact is a markdown file tagged with the release train and staged in the public changelog repo.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Last-minute Runtime performance regression discovered during soak. Mitigation: hold a dedicated fast-response debugging shift and a rollback window; maintain a compatible model variant as fallback.
Risk: Docs or release notes miss breaking behavior. Mitigation: mandatory engineering sign-off and pre-release external review by Solutions Engineering.
Risk: Console telemetry mismatch causes billing confusion. Mitigation: run parallel data-validation and communicate temporary rate-limit safeguards to customers.
Risk: GTM dependencies slip (blog, SDK). Mitigation: surface blockers in weekly GTM sync and identify minimum viable comms for launch.
